title: ASICs, CPUs, GPUs, and open-source tools
outcome: Match hardware and software to a chain and a job.
show: Build a reference card with three columns labeled hardware, mining software or firmware, and verifying software.
concepts: ASICs are designed for a specific workload. Bitcoin’s SHA-256d mining is ordinarily performed by dedicated ASICs.

A general-purpose CPU handles varied workloads. A GPU excels at parallel computation. Suitability depends on the chain’s algorithm, and hardware capability by itself says little about economic viability.
Explore Bitaxe ESP-Miner firmware, Bitcoin Core node software, and the Stratum V2 Reference Implementation. Record the role of each before selecting a setup for practice.
replicate: Pick a source repository. Identify what it runs on, what input it expects, and what output you can independently check.
Describe where a pool account and a local miner belong on the card without collecting real classmates’ credentials.
check: Which tool validates the blockchain in this example?
Bitcoin Core is full-node software. ESP-Miner firmware runs compatible Bitaxe hardware, and the Stratum implementation handles mining communications.
